Fleet Finch cleanup trials: rolling log
=======================================

What this is: a running record of every command sent to the test iPad while stock
launch services are removed one at a time, what came back, and what was decided.
It is appended to as the work goes, so the end of the file is the latest state.

How to read it:
  - Times at the left are the computer's clock (MST). Times inside iPad output are
    the iPad's own clock.
  - DO      a command sent to the iPad over SSH; the lines under it starting "$" are
            the exact command, the lines starting "|" are everything it printed.
  - RESULT  how that command ended and how long it took.
  - NOTE    what I did on the computer, or what I concluded.
  - TRIAL   the start or end of one service's trial.
  - VERDICT the outcome for one service.
  - ALARM   contact with the iPad was lost, or something looked wrong.
  - Raw captures (the iPad's own log stream, heartbeat timings, the on-device
    recorder's files) are kept in ~/.fleetfinch/cleanup-trials/raw on the computer
    and named here when they matter.

Background, 2026-11-26 morning: removing 70 stock and hidden apps worked and survived
a restart. Then one command unloaded and deleted 14 launch services at once
(identityservicesd, imagent, imautomatichistorydeletionagent, imavagent,
imtransferagent, IMLoggingAgent, IDSCredentialsAgent, IDSRemoteURLConnectionAgent,
cmfsyncagent, callservicesd, CallHistorySyncHelper, recentsd,
idskeychainsyncingproxy, absd). About 20 seconds later the iPad stopped answering
SSH (it still answered ping and accepted connections on port 22, but sent no banner),
stayed that way through a restart, and was factory restored. No log of those
seconds survived. This log exists so that cannot happen again.

2026-11-26 13:59:47  NOTE    Wrote the on-device guard (source kept at ~/.fleetfinch/cleanup-trials/src/ffguard.c). It is a root process at fixed top user priority that every 2 s records load, process count, starts and exits, launchd's CPU share and the busiest processes to /var/root/ffguard/record.log; every 10 s times an SSH banner on port 22, a banner on its own second sshd on port 2222 (started without launchd), 'launchctl list' and a plain program start; copies the raw system log to /var/root/ffguard/syslog.log; and, when armed, if the computer's heartbeat (a new SSH login every 4 s touching /var/root/ffguard/beat) stops for 75 s (240 s after a start), puts back whatever is on trial and restarts the iPad; if that start gets no heartbeat either, it puts back everything set aside and restarts once more, then stands down.

2026-11-26 21:21:52  NOTE    SUMMARY OF THE EVENING'S SLEEP FAULT. Symptom: from 19:43:31 the iPad, on battery and with the guard gone, could not be reached at all for 53 minutes. Cause: iOS switches the Wi-Fi chip off for a sleep unless a program has asked wifid to keep it joined ('WoW'); on the stock system apsd asks, but only while other services are registered with it; with the list removed nothing asks. It was hidden all afternoon because the guard held the iPad awake. Not the fault of any one service: apsd put back alone quits after 17 s. Fix: Fleet Finch asks for it itself (launch service com.fleetfinch.app.reach runs 'fleetfinch keep-reachable', tool/FFStayJoined.m). Tested: nap with the request (banner on every try), 18 minutes asleep without a packet from the computer (answered on the first try), a restart (the service came up by itself, the helper passed batches 7 and 8), and asleep with no harness at all (answered). apsd stays on the removal list. Known and unchanged from stock: on battery a connection that arrives in the instant the iPad falls asleep can time out once; the next try is answered. Not tested: a sleep on battery longer than 18 minutes, the whole list put back at once, iPhone width, other models.
